1... /**
2...  * Snowflake query helper. Call from any server component or route handler:
3...  *   const rows = await querySnowflake("SELECT ...")
4...  *   const rows = await querySnowflake("SELECT ...", { callersRights: true })
5...  *   const rows = await querySnowflake("SELECT ...", { warehouse: "MY_WH" })
6...  *
7...  * Variable binding (recommended for any user-supplied values — prevents SQL injection):
8...  *   const rows = await querySnowflake(
9...  *     "SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ? AND status = ?",
10...  *     { binds: [id, status] },
11...  *   )
12...  *   Use `?` placeholders in the SQL and pass values via the `binds` option. Binds are
13...  *   supported on both helpers and on queryWithToken(...). See the Snowflake SDK docs for
14...  *   supported bind value types.
15...  *
16...  * Which helper to use:
17...  *   - querySnowflake — default for simple, fast queries (small lookups, tight filters,
18...  *     typically well under ~10 seconds end-to-end).
19...  *   - querySnowflakeLongRunning — use when the work may exceed ~10 seconds or is
20...  *     warehouse-heavy (large scans, big aggregations, COPY/EXPORT, long-running
21...  *     procedures, resuming warehouse, etc.). Submits async, polls by query id, then
22...  *     fetches rows:
23...  *       const rows = await querySnowflakeLongRunning("CALL MY_LONG_JOB(...)")
24...  *   Same auth options (callersRights, pools) apply to both.
25...  *
26...  * Logging: by default prints concise lines (auth path, timing, truncated SQL, queryId on
27...  * success). Set SNOWFLAKE_SDK_QUIET=1 to disable. SDK internal logs stay at ERROR unless
28...  * you change snowflake.configure below.
29...  *
30...  * Auth is auto-detected (in priority order):
31...  *   1. SPCS token file (/snowflake/session/token) — read fresh on every call
32...  *   2. SNOWFLAKE_USER + SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD env vars — password auth (local dev)
33...  *   3. ~/.snowflake/config.toml default connection — zero-config local dev
34...  *
35...  * Connection pooling:
36...  *   Owner's rights: single pool per process, recreated when the service token rotates.
37...  *   Caller's rights: one pool per user+role (keyed by combined token), all drained
38...  *     when the service token rotates.
39...  *   Local dev pools (password / toml) are shared and never rotated.
40...  *
41...  * SPCS caller's rights helpers:
42...  *   queryWithToken(query, token) — runs a query with an explicit OAuth token.
43...  *   getServiceToken() — reads the SPCS service token from /snowflake/session/token.
44...  *   buildCallerRightsToken(callerUserToken) — combines service + caller tokens.
45...  *
46...  * Secrets:
47...  *   getSecret(name, type) — reads a Snowflake SECRET value at runtime. Use this instead of
48...  *     reading SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_* env vars or querying the SECRET object directly (see the
49...  *     getSecret docstring below). The secret must be declared under `secrets:` in app.yml to
50...  *     be available in SPCS.
51...  *
52...  * Cleanup:
53...  *   closePool() — drains and destroys all active pools on shutdown.
54...  */
55... 
56... import { headers } from "next/headers"
57... import fs from "fs"
58... import path from "path"
59... import os from "os"
60... import snowflake from "snowflake-sdk"
61... 
62... snowflake.configure({
63...   logLevel: "ERROR",
64...   ...(process.env.SNOWFLAKE_SDK_DISABLE_OCSP === "true" && { disableOCSPChecks: true, ocspFailOpen: true }),
65... })
66... 
67... const SPCS_TOKEN_PATH = "/snowflake/session/token"
68... 
69... const LOG_PREFIX = "[snowflake]"
70... 
71... /** Single-line SQL preview for logs (keeps log volume small). */
72... function previewSql(sql: string, maxLen = 200): string {
73...   const s = sql.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()
74...   if (s.length <= maxLen) return s
75...   return `${s.slice(0, maxLen)}…`
76... }
77... 
78... function sfLogQuiet(): boolean {
79...   const v = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_SDK_QUIET
80...   return v === "1" || v === "true"
81... }
82... 
83... function sfLog(message: string): void {
84...   if (sfLogQuiet()) return
85...   console.log(`${LOG_PREFIX} ${message}`)
86... }
87... 
88... function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
89...   return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))
90... }
91... 
92... /**
93...  * Build the `parameters` fragment for `conn.execute` when a per-query warehouse
94...  * override is requested. Sets the QUERY_WAREHOUSE_NAME statement parameter so the
95...  * query runs on the given warehouse without a separate `USE WAREHOUSE` round-trip.
96...  */
97... function warehouseParams(warehouse?: string): { parameters?: Record<string, unknown> } {
98...   return warehouse ? { parameters: { QUERY_WAREHOUSE_NAME: warehouse } } : {}
99... }
100... 
101... /** SDK bind values for `?` placeholders. Kept as its own type since @types may lag. */
102... type Binds = snowflake.Binds
103... 
104... /** Build the `binds` fragment for `conn.execute` when bind values are provided. */
105... function bindParams(binds?: Binds): { binds?: Binds } {
106...   return binds && binds.length > 0 ? { binds } : {}
107... }
108... 
109... /** The SDK supports these; @types/snowflake-sdk may lag — keep cast at boundary. */
110... type PollingConnection = snowflake.Connection & {
111...   getQueryStatus: (queryId: string) => Promise<string>
112...   getResultsFromQueryId: (opts: { queryId: string }) => Promise<{ streamRows: () => NodeJS.ReadableStream }>
113...   isStillRunning: (status: string) => boolean
114...   isAnError: (status: string) => boolean
115...   getQueryStatusThrowIfError: (queryId: string) => Promise<string>
116... }
117... 
118... type ExecuteOptions = Parameters<snowflake.Connection["execute"]>[0] & { asyncExec?: boolean }
119... 
120... function streamRowsToArray(statement: { streamRows: () => NodeJS.ReadableStream }): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
121...   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
122...     const rows: Record<string, any>[] = []
123...     statement
124...       .streamRows()
125...       .on("error", (err: Error) => reject(err))
126...       .on("data", (row: Record<string, any>) => rows.push(row))
127...       .on("end", () => resolve(rows))
128...   })
129... }
130... 
131... /**
132...  * Submit `asyncExec`, poll `getQueryStatus` until the warehouse finishes, then fetch rows.
133...  * Keeps status logs sparse (default: at most once per minute while running).
134...  */
135... async function runLongRunningOnConnection(
136...   conn: PollingConnection,
137...   query: string,
138...   options: {
139...     pollIntervalMs: number
140...     statusLogIntervalMs: number
141...     maxWaitMs?: number
142...   },
143...   warehouse?: string,
144...   binds?: Binds,
145... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
146...   const queryId = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
147...     conn.execute({
148...       sqlText: query,
149...       asyncExec: true,
150...       ...warehouseParams(warehouse),
151...       ...bindParams(binds),
152...       complete: (err, stmt) => {
153...         if (err) reject(new Error(`Async submit failed: ${err.message}`))
154...         else resolve(stmt!.getQueryId())
155...       },
156...     } as ExecuteOptions)
157...   })
158... 
159...   const t0 = Date.now()
160...   sfLog(`long-running submitted queryId=${queryId} sql=${JSON.stringify(previewSql(query))}`)
161... 
162...   let lastStatusLog = t0
163...   while (true) {
164...     if (options.maxWaitMs !== undefined && Date.now() - t0 > options.maxWaitMs) {
165...       throw new Error(
166...         `Long-running query timed out after ${options.maxWaitMs}ms (queryId=${queryId})`,
167...       )
168...     }
169... 
170...     const status = await conn.getQueryStatus(queryId)
171...     if (conn.isAnError(status)) {
172...       try {
173...         await conn.getQueryStatusThrowIfError(queryId)
174...       } catch (e) {
175...         const msg = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)
176...         throw new Error(`Query failed (queryId=${queryId}): ${msg}`)
177...       }
178...       throw new Error(`Query failed (queryId=${queryId}): ${status}`)
179...     }
180...     if (!conn.isStillRunning(status)) break
181... 
182...     const now = Date.now()
183...     if (now - lastStatusLog >= options.statusLogIntervalMs) {
184...       sfLog(
185...         `long-running poll queryId=${queryId} status=${status} elapsedMs=${now - t0}`,
186...       )
187...       lastStatusLog = now
188...     }
189...     await sleep(options.pollIntervalMs)
190...   }
191... 
192...   const statement = await conn.getResultsFromQueryId({ queryId })
193...   const rows = await streamRowsToArray(statement)
194...   sfLog(
195...     `long-running complete queryId=${queryId} rows=${rows.length} totalMs=${Date.now() - t0}`,
196...   )
197...   return rows
198... }
199... 
200... // --- Connection pool configuration ---
201... 
202... const POOL_CONFIG = {
203...   min: 0, // Start with no connections (lazy init)
204...   max: 10, // Scale up to 10 concurrent connections
205... }
206... 
207... // Owner's rights: single pool, recreated when the service token rotates.
208... let ownersPool: ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> | null = null
209... let ownersPoolToken = ""
210... 
211... // Caller's rights: one pool per combined token (user+role), keyed by combined token.
212... // All pools are drained when the service token rotates.
213... const callersPool = new Map<string, ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool>>()
214... let callersServiceToken = ""
215... 
216... // Local dev pools.
217... let passwordPool: ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> | null = null
218... let tomlPool: ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> | null = null
219... 
220... function baseConfig(): snowflake.ConnectionOptions {
221...   const application = "SnowflakeAppRuntime"
222...   const base: snowflake.ConnectionOptions = { application }
223...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT) base.account = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT
224...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE) base.warehouse = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE
225...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_URL) base.accessUrl = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT_URL
226...   // SNOWFLAKE_HOST is commonly injected by eval/CI frameworks
227...   if (!base.accessUrl && process.env.SNOWFLAKE_HOST) {
228...     base.accessUrl = `https://${process.env.SNOWFLAKE_HOST}`
229...   }
230...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_ROLE) base.role = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_ROLE
231...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE) base.database = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE
232...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA) base.schema = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA
233...   return base
234... }
235... 
236... // --- ~/.snowflake/connections.toml + config.toml reader ---
237... 
238... interface TomlConnection {
239...   account?: string
240...   user?: string
241...   password?: string
242...   host?: string
243...   port?: string | number
244...   warehouse?: string
245...   database?: string
246...   schema?: string
247...   region?: string
248...   role?: string
249...   authenticator?: string
250...   protocol?: string
251...   token_file_path?: string
252...   [key: string]: unknown
253... }
254... 
255... let _tomlConfigCache: { defaultName: string; connections: Record<string, TomlConnection> } | null | undefined
256... 
257... function normalizeConnectionsToml(doc: Record<string, any>): Record<string, TomlConnection> {
258...   const result: Record<string, TomlConnection> = {}
259...   for (const [key, val] of Object.entries(doc)) {
260...     if (key === "default_connection_name" || key === "connections") continue
261...     if (typeof val === "object" && val !== null && !Array.isArray(val)) {
262...       result[key] = val as TomlConnection
263...     }
264...   }
265...   if (typeof doc.connections === "object" && doc.connections !== null && !Array.isArray(doc.connections)) {
266...     Object.assign(result, doc.connections as Record<string, TomlConnection>)
267...   }
268...   return result
269... }
270... 
271... /**
272...  * Resolve a Snowflake connection from local TOML config files.
273...  *
274...  * Tries two file layouts (in order):
275...  *   1. ~/.snowflake/connections.toml — supports both nested ([connections.name])
276...  *      and legacy (top-level [name]) formats; nested wins on conflict.
277...  *   2. ~/.snowflake/config.toml — connections nested under [connections.*] sections.
278...  *
279...  * Both files may contain a `default_connection_name` key. The env var
280...  * SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_NAME takes priority, then SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME
281...  * (set by Cortex Code for SnowCLI compatibility), then the file-level default.
282...  *
283...  * Result is cached for the lifetime of the process.
284...  */
285... export function readTomlDefaultConnection(): TomlConnection | null {
286...   if (_tomlConfigCache === undefined) {
287...     _tomlConfigCache = null // mark as attempted
288...     try {
289...       // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports
290...       const { parse } = require("smol-toml") as { parse: (s: string) => Record<string, any> }
291...       const snowDir = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_HOME ?? path.join(os.homedir(), ".snowflake")
292... 
293...       let defaultName = ""
294...       let connections: Record<string, TomlConnection> = {}
295... 
296...       // connections.toml: top-level sections are connections
297...       const connPath = path.join(snowDir, "connections.toml")
298...       if (fs.existsSync(connPath)) {
299...         const doc = parse(fs.readFileSync(connPath, "utf8"))
300...         if (typeof doc.default_connection_name === "string") defaultName = doc.default_connection_name
301...         connections = normalizeConnectionsToml(doc)
302...       }
303... 
304...       // config.toml: connections nested under [connections.*], also has default_connection_name
305...       const configPath = path.join(snowDir, "config.toml")
306...       if (fs.existsSync(configPath)) {
307...         const doc = parse(fs.readFileSync(configPath, "utf8"))
308...         if (!defaultName && typeof doc.default_connection_name === "string") {
309...           defaultName = doc.default_connection_name
310...         }
311...         // Only use config.toml connections if connections.toml had none
312...         if (Object.keys(connections).length === 0) {
313...           connections = (doc.connections ?? {}) as Record<string, TomlConnection>
314...         }
315...       }
316... 
317...       // General SNOWFLAKE_<KEY> env vars overlay on every toml connection (spec §3.B)
318...       const envOverlay: Partial<TomlConnection> = {}
319...       const CONN_KEYS = new Set(["account","user","password","database","schema","role","warehouse","protocol","host","port","region","authenticator"])
320...       for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(process.env)) {
321...         if (!k.startsWith("SNOWFLAKE_") || k === "SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_NAME" || k === "SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME" || k === "SNOWFLAKE_HOME") continue
322...         const field = k.slice("SNOWFLAKE_".length).toLowerCase()
323...         if (CONN_KEYS.has(field)) (envOverlay as Record<string, string>)[field] = v!
324...       }
325...       if (Object.keys(envOverlay).length > 0) {
326...         for (const name of Object.keys(connections)) {
327...           connections[name] = { ...connections[name], ...envOverlay }
328...         }
329...       }
330... 
331...       // SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_NAME overrides file-level default
332...       if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_NAME) {
333...         defaultName = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTION_NAME
334...       } else if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME) {
335...         defaultName = process.env.SNOWFLAKE_DEFAULT_CONNECTION_NAME
336...       }
337... 
338...       _tomlConfigCache = { defaultName, connections }
339...     } catch {
340...       // parse error or smol-toml not installed — silently skip
341...       return null
342...     }
343...   }
344... 
345...   if (!_tomlConfigCache) return null
346... 
347...   const { defaultName, connections } = _tomlConfigCache
348...   const names = Object.keys(connections)
349...   if (names.length === 0) return null
350... 
351...   const conn = (defaultName && connections[defaultName]) || connections[names[0]]
352...   return conn ?? null
353... }
354... 
355... /** Reset the connection config cache. Exported for testing only. */
356... export function resetTomlConfigCache() {
357...   _tomlConfigCache = undefined
358... }
359... 
360... function tomlConnectionConfig(conn: TomlConnection): snowflake.ConnectionOptions {
361...   // Use SDK's normalizeConnectionOptions for snake_case -> camelCase + key aliases
362...   // Type assertion needed until @types/snowflake-sdk includes normalizeConnectionOptions
363...   const normalize = (snowflake as unknown as { normalizeConnectionOptions: (o: Record<string, unknown>) => snowflake.ConnectionOptions }).normalizeConnectionOptions
364...   const normalized = normalize(conn as Record<string, unknown>)
365...   // SDK doesn't handle host/port/protocol -> accessUrl, so we do it here
366...   if (conn.host && !normalized.accessUrl) {
367...     const protocol = conn.protocol ?? "https"
368...     const port = conn.port ? `:${conn.port}` : ""
369...     normalized.accessUrl = `${protocol}://${conn.host}${port}`
370...   }
371...   // The SDK only reads token_file_path when it loads the TOML itself
372...   // (createConnection with no options). Because we build the options object and
373...   // pass it to createConnection/createPool, the SDK ignores token_file_path and
374...   // sends an empty OAuth token, which the server rejects with error 390303.
375...   // So read the token file ourselves for plain "oauth" auth.
376...   if (
377...     !normalized.token &&
378...     typeof normalized.authenticator === "string" &&
379...     normalized.authenticator.toUpperCase() === "OAUTH" &&
380...     conn.token_file_path
381...   ) {
382...     normalized.token = fs.readFileSync(conn.token_file_path, "utf8").trim()
383...   }
384...   return normalized
385... }
386... 
387... // --- Pool helpers ---
388... 
389... function getOwnersPool(serviceToken: string): ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> {
390...   if (ownersPool && ownersPoolToken !== serviceToken) {
391...     sfLog("pool: draining owner's-rights pool (SPCS service token rotated)")
392...     ownersPool.drain()
393...     ownersPool = null
394...   }
395...   if (!ownersPool) {
396...     sfLog("pool: creating owner's-rights OAuth pool (SPCS)")
397...     ownersPool = snowflake.createPool(
398...       { ...baseConfig(), authenticator: "OAUTH", token: serviceToken },
399...       POOL_CONFIG,
400...     )
401...     ownersPoolToken = serviceToken
402...   }
403...   return ownersPool
404... }
405... 
406... function getCallersPool(combinedToken: string, serviceToken: string): ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> {
407...   // Service token rotated — all combined tokens are stale, drain everything.
408...   if (callersServiceToken !== serviceToken) {
409...     if (callersPool.size > 0) {
410...       sfLog(`pool: draining ${callersPool.size} caller's-rights pool(s) (SPCS service token rotated)`)
411...     }
412...     for (const pool of callersPool.values()) pool.drain()
413...     callersPool.clear()
414...     callersServiceToken = serviceToken
415...   }
416...   if (!callersPool.has(combinedToken)) {
417...     sfLog("pool: creating caller's-rights OAuth pool (SPCS)")
418...     callersPool.set(
419...       combinedToken,
420...       snowflake.createPool(
421...         { ...baseConfig(), authenticator: "OAUTH", token: combinedToken },
422...         POOL_CONFIG,
423...       ),
424...     )
425...   }
426...   return callersPool.get(combinedToken)!
427... }
428... 
429... function getPasswordPool(): ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> {
430...   if (!passwordPool) {
431...     sfLog("pool: creating password-auth pool (SNOWFLAKE_USER)")
432...     passwordPool = snowflake.createPool(
433...       {
434...         ...baseConfig(),
435...         username: process.env.SNOWFLAKE_USER,
436...         password: process.env.SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD,
437...       },
438...       POOL_CONFIG,
439...     )
440...   }
441...   return passwordPool
442... }
443... 
444... function getTomlPool(conn: TomlConnection): ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool> {
445...   if (!tomlPool) {
446...     sfLog("pool: creating TOML default-connection pool (~/.snowflake)")
447...     tomlPool = snowflake.createPool({ ...tomlConnectionConfig(conn), ...baseConfig() }, POOL_CONFIG)
448...   }
449...   return tomlPool
450... }
451... 
452... function queryWithPool(
453...   pool: ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool>,
454...   query: string,
455...   authTag: string,
456...   warehouse?: string,
457...   binds?: Binds,
458... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
459...   return pool.use(async (conn) => {
460...     const t0 = Date.now()
461...     sfLog(`query start mode=${authTag} sql=${JSON.stringify(previewSql(query))}`)
462...     return new Promise<Record<string, any>[]>((res, rej) => {
463...       conn.execute({
464...         sqlText: query,
465...         ...warehouseParams(warehouse),
466...         ...bindParams(binds),
467...         complete: (err, stmt, rows) => {
468...           const ms = Date.now() - t0
469...           const qid =
470...             stmt && typeof stmt.getQueryId === "function" ? ` queryId=${stmt.getQueryId()}` : ""
471...           if (err) {
472...             sfLog(`query error mode=${authTag} afterMs=${ms}${qid}: ${err.message}`)
473...             rej(new Error(`Query failed: ${err.message}`))
474...           } else {
475...             const out = (rows ?? []) as Record<string, any>[]
476...             sfLog(`query ok mode=${authTag} rows=${out.length} afterMs=${ms}${qid}`)
477...             res(out)
478...           }
479...         },
480...       })
481...     })
482...   })
483... }
484... 
485... function queryWithPoolLongRunning(
486...   pool: ReturnType<typeof snowflake.createPool>,
487...   query: string,
488...   authTag: string,
489...   longOpts: { pollIntervalMs: number; statusLogIntervalMs: number; maxWaitMs?: number },
490...   warehouse?: string,
491...   binds?: Binds,
492... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
493...   return pool.use(async (conn) => {
494...     sfLog(`long-running start mode=${authTag} sql=${JSON.stringify(previewSql(query))}`)
495...     return runLongRunningOnConnection(conn as unknown as PollingConnection, query, longOpts, warehouse, binds)
496...   })
497... }
498... 
499... // --- One-shot connection helper (used for per-request tokens) ---
500... 
501... function connectAndQuery(
502...   config: snowflake.ConnectionOptions,
503...   query: string,
504...   authTag: string,
505...   warehouse?: string,
506...   binds?: Binds,
507... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
508...   const conn = snowflake.createConnection(config)
509...   const t0 = Date.now()
510...   sfLog(`query start mode=${authTag} (one-shot) sql=${JSON.stringify(previewSql(query))}`)
511...   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
512...     conn.connect((err) => {
513...       if (err) {
514...         sfLog(`connect failed mode=${authTag}: ${err.message}`)
515...         return reject(new Error(`Snowflake connection failed: ${err.message}`))
516...       }
517...       conn.execute({
518...         sqlText: query,
519...         ...warehouseParams(warehouse),
520...         ...bindParams(binds),
521...         complete: (err, stmt, rows) => {
522...           conn.destroy(() => {})
523...           const ms = Date.now() - t0
524...           const qid =
525...             stmt && typeof stmt.getQueryId === "function" ? ` queryId=${stmt.getQueryId()}` : ""
526...           if (err) {
527...             sfLog(`query error mode=${authTag} afterMs=${ms}${qid}: ${err.message}`)
528...             reject(new Error(`Query failed: ${err.message}`))
529...           } else {
530...             const out = (rows ?? []) as Record<string, any>[]
531...             sfLog(`query ok mode=${authTag} rows=${out.length} afterMs=${ms}${qid}`)
532...             resolve(out)
533...           }
534...         },
535...       })
536...     })
537...   })
538... }
539... 
540... function connectAndQueryLongRunning(
541...   config: snowflake.ConnectionOptions,
542...   query: string,
543...   authTag: string,
544...   longOpts: { pollIntervalMs: number; statusLogIntervalMs: number; maxWaitMs?: number },
545...   warehouse?: string,
546...   binds?: Binds,
547... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
548...   const conn = snowflake.createConnection(config)
549...   const t0 = Date.now()
550...   sfLog(`long-running start mode=${authTag} (one-shot) sql=${JSON.stringify(previewSql(query))}`)
551...   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
552...     conn.connect((err) => {
553...       if (err) {
554...         sfLog(`connect failed mode=${authTag}: ${err.message}`)
555...         return reject(new Error(`Snowflake connection failed: ${err.message}`))
556...       }
557...       runLongRunningOnConnection(conn as unknown as PollingConnection, query, longOpts, warehouse, binds)
558...         .then((rows) => {
559...           conn.destroy(() => {})
560...           sfLog(`long-running one-shot done mode=${authTag} totalMs=${Date.now() - t0}`)
561...           resolve(rows)
562...         })
563...         .catch((e) => {
564...           conn.destroy(() => {})
565...           reject(e)
566...         })
567...     })
568...   })
569... }
570... 
571... interface QueryOptions {
572...   callersRights?: boolean
573...   /**
574...    * Run this query on a specific warehouse. Sets the QUERY_WAREHOUSE_NAME
575...    * statement parameter for the execution. When omitted, the connection's
576...    * default warehouse is used.
577...    */
578...   warehouse?: string
579...   /**
580...    * Bind values for `?` placeholders in the SQL. Use this for any user-supplied
581...    * values to avoid SQL injection, e.g.
582...    *   querySnowflake("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ?", { binds: [id] })
583...    */
584...   binds?: Binds
585... }
586... 
587... /** Extra options for `querySnowflakeLongRunning` / `queryWithTokenLongRunning`. */
588... export interface LongRunningQueryOptions extends QueryOptions {
589...   /**
590...    * How often to call GS while the query is running (default 5000).
591...    * Kept conservative to limit log volume and API chatter.
592...    */
593...   pollIntervalMs?: number
594...   /**
595...    * While running, emit at most one `[snowflake] long-running poll …` line per this many ms (default 60000).
596...    */
597...   statusLogIntervalMs?: number
598...   /** Fail if the query is still not finished after this many ms (optional). */
599...   maxWaitMs?: number
600... }
601... 
602... function resolveLongRunningOpts(
603...   o: LongRunningQueryOptions,
604... ): { pollIntervalMs: number; statusLogIntervalMs: number; maxWaitMs?: number } {
605...   return {
606...     pollIntervalMs: o.pollIntervalMs ?? 5000,
607...     statusLogIntervalMs: o.statusLogIntervalMs ?? 60_000,
608...     maxWaitMs: o.maxWaitMs,
609...   }
610... }
611... 
612... export async function querySnowflake(query: string, options: QueryOptions = {}): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
613...   const { callersRights = false, warehouse, binds } = options
614...   const serviceToken = getServiceToken()
615... 
616...   if (serviceToken) {
617...     if (callersRights) {
618...       const callerToken = (await headers()).get("sf-context-current-user-token") ?? ""
619...       if (!callerToken) {
620...         throw new Error(
621...           "No sf-context-current-user-token header. Ensure the app is running in SPCS with caller's rights enabled.",
622...         )
623...       }
624...       const combinedToken = serviceToken + "." + callerToken
625...       return queryWithPool(getCallersPool(combinedToken, serviceToken), query, "spcs-caller", warehouse, binds)
626...     }
627...     // Retry once on terminated connection (service token rotated mid-flight).
628...     try {
629...       return await queryWithPool(getOwnersPool(serviceToken), query, "spcs-owner", warehouse, binds)
630...     } catch (err) {
631...       const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
632...       if (msg.includes("terminated connection")) {
633...         sfLog("query retry: terminated connection — clearing owner pool and retrying once")
634...         ownersPool?.drain()
635...         ownersPool = null
636...         return queryWithPool(getOwnersPool(serviceToken), query, "spcs-owner", warehouse, binds)
637...       }
638...       throw err
639...     }
640...   }
641... 
642...   // Local dev: no SPCS token, so caller's rights is not possible.
643...   if (callersRights) {
644...     console.warn("[snowflake] useCallersRights=true has no effect outside SPCS — using local dev credentials")
645...   }
646... 
647...   // Explicit env vars: password auth via pooled connections
648...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_USER && process.env.SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD) {
649...     return queryWithPool(getPasswordPool(), query, "password", warehouse, binds)
650...   }
651... 
652...   // ~/.snowflake/connections.toml or config.toml: use the default connection (local dev)
653...   const tomlConn = readTomlDefaultConnection()
654...   if (tomlConn) {
655...     return queryWithPool(getTomlPool(tomlConn), query, "toml", warehouse, binds)
656...   }
657... 
658...   throw new Error(
659...     "No Snowflake credentials found. Provide one of:\n" +
660...     "  1. SPCS token file at /snowflake/session/token\n" +
661...     "  2. SNOWFLAKE_USER + SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD env vars\n" +
662...       "  3. ~/.snowflake/config.toml with a default connection"
663...   )
664... }
665... 
666... /**
667...  * Same auth and pooling as {@link querySnowflake}, but submits with `asyncExec`, then polls
668...  * by `queryId` until the statement finishes (intended for queries that often exceed ~1 minute).
669...  */
670... export async function querySnowflakeLongRunning(
671...   query: string,
672...   options: LongRunningQueryOptions = {},
673... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
674...   const { callersRights = false, warehouse, binds, ...longRest } = options
675...   const longOpts = resolveLongRunningOpts({ callersRights, ...longRest })
676...   const serviceToken = getServiceToken()
677... 
678...   if (serviceToken) {
679...     if (callersRights) {
680...       const callerToken = (await headers()).get("sf-context-current-user-token") ?? ""
681...       if (!callerToken) {
682...         throw new Error(
683...           "No sf-context-current-user-token header. Ensure the app is running in SPCS with caller's rights enabled.",
684...         )
685...       }
686...       const combinedToken = serviceToken + "." + callerToken
687...       return queryWithPoolLongRunning(
688...         getCallersPool(combinedToken, serviceToken),
689...         query,
690...         "spcs-caller",
691...         longOpts,
692...         warehouse,
693...         binds,
694...       )
695...     }
696...     return queryWithPoolLongRunning(getOwnersPool(serviceToken), query, "spcs-owner", longOpts, warehouse, binds)
697...   }
698... 
699...   if (callersRights) {
700...     console.warn("[snowflake] useCallersRights=true has no effect outside SPCS — using local dev credentials")
701...   }
702... 
703...   if (process.env.SNOWFLAKE_USER && process.env.SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD) {
704...     return queryWithPoolLongRunning(getPasswordPool(), query, "password", longOpts, warehouse, binds)
705...   }
706... 
707...   const tomlConn = readTomlDefaultConnection()
708...   if (tomlConn) {
709...     return queryWithPoolLongRunning(getTomlPool(tomlConn), query, "toml", longOpts, warehouse, binds)
710...   }
711... 
712...   throw new Error(
713...     "No Snowflake credentials found. Provide one of:\n" +
714...     "  1. SPCS token file at /snowflake/session/token\n" +
715...     "  2. SNOWFLAKE_USER + SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD env vars\n" +
716...     "  3. ~/.snowflake/config.toml with a default connection"
717...   )
718... }
719... 
720... // --- SPCS caller's rights helpers ---
721... 
722... export function getServiceToken(): string {
723...   try {
724...     return fs.readFileSync(SPCS_TOKEN_PATH, "utf8").trim()
725...   } catch {
726...     return ""
727...   }
728... }
729... 
730... export function buildCallerRightsToken(callerUserToken: string): string {
731...   const serviceToken = getServiceToken()
732...   if (!serviceToken) {
733...     throw new Error("No SPCS service token available at " + SPCS_TOKEN_PATH)
734...   }
735...   return serviceToken + "." + callerUserToken
736... }
737... 
738... /**
739...  * Run a query using an explicit OAuth token (for service-rights or caller's-rights).
740...  * Creates a fresh connection each time since the token may differ per request.
741...  * Pass `warehouse` to run the query on a specific warehouse (QUERY_WAREHOUSE_NAME).
742...  * Pass `binds` for `?` placeholder values (recommended for user-supplied input).
743...  */
744... export async function queryWithToken(
745...   query: string,
746...   token: string,
747...   warehouse?: string,
748...   binds?: Binds,
749... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
750...   return connectAndQuery({ ...baseConfig(), authenticator: "OAUTH", token }, query, "oauth-token", warehouse, binds)
751... }
752... 
753... /**
754...  * One-shot OAuth connection: async submit + poll + fetch (see {@link querySnowflakeLongRunning}).
755...  */
756... export async function queryWithTokenLongRunning(
757...   query: string,
758...   token: string,
759...   options: Omit<LongRunningQueryOptions, "callersRights"> = {},
760... ): Promise<Record<string, any>[]> {
761...   const { warehouse, binds, ...longRest } = options
762...   const longOpts = resolveLongRunningOpts({ callersRights: false, ...longRest })
763...   return connectAndQueryLongRunning(
764...     { ...baseConfig(), authenticator: "OAUTH", token },
765...     query,
766...     "oauth-token",
767...     longOpts,
768...     warehouse,
769...     binds,
770...   )
771... }
772... 
773... // --- Secrets ---
774... 
775... /**
776...  * Snowflake secret types supported by {@link getSecret}. Mirrors the `TYPE` of a
777...  * Snowflake `SECRET` object. (`GENERIC_STRING`, `PASSWORD`, and `OAUTH2` are supported.)
778...  */
779... export enum SecretType {
780...   /** Single opaque string (e.g. an API key). `getSecret` returns the string. */
781...   GENERIC_STRING = "GENERIC_STRING",
782...   /** Username + password pair. `getSecret` returns `{ username, password }`. */
783...   PASSWORD = "PASSWORD",
784...   /** OAuth2 access token. `getSecret` returns a `Promise<string>` — see the docstring. */
785...   OAUTH2 = "OAUTH2",
786... }
787... 
788... /** Value returned for a {@link SecretType.PASSWORD} secret. */
789... export interface PasswordSecret {
790...   username: string
791...   password: string
792... }
793... 
794... /** Directory where SPCS mounts declared secrets (one subdirectory per secret). */
795... const SPCS_SECRETS_DIR = "/secrets"
796... 
797... /** `SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_<FIELD>` — the env var the runtime injects (name upper-cased). */
798... function secretEnvVarName(name: string, field: string): string {
799...   return `SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_${name.toUpperCase()}_${field}`
800... }
801... 
802... /** Read a mounted secret file (SPCS) if present and non-empty; otherwise null. */
803... function readMountedSecretFile(name: string, file: string): string | null {
804...   const filePath = path.join(SPCS_SECRETS_DIR, name, file)
805...   try {
806...     const contents = fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf8")
807...     if (typeof contents === "string" && contents.trim() !== "") {
808...       return contents.trim()
809...     }
810...   } catch {
811...     // File not mounted (e.g. local dev).
812...   }
813...   return null
814... }
815... 
816... /**
817...  * Read one field of a secret.
818...  *
819...  * In SPCS the runtime mounts each declared secret as files under
820...  * `/secrets/<name>/<field>`. We read that file first, and fall back to the
821...  * `SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_<FIELD>` env var (upper-case) for local development
822...  * where no files are mounted.
823...  *
824...  * @param name  Logical secret name (matches app.yml `secrets[].name`).
825...  * @param file  Mounted file name (lower-case), e.g. `secret_string`, `username`, `password`.
826...  * @param env   Env var field suffix (upper-case), e.g. `SECRET_STRING`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD`.
827...  */
828... function readSecretField(name: string, file: string, env: string): string {
829...   // 1. Mounted secret file (SPCS): /secrets/<name>/<file>
830...   const mounted = readMountedSecretFile(name, file)
831...   if (mounted !== null) return mounted
832... 
833...   // 2. Env var fallback (local dev): SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_<FIELD>
834...   const envVar = secretEnvVarName(name, env)
835...   const value = process.env[envVar]
836...   if (value) return value
837... 
838...   throw new Error(
839...     `Secret "${name}" field "${file}" is not available. Expected the mounted file ` +
840...       `${path.join(SPCS_SECRETS_DIR, name, file)} (SPCS) or the env var ${envVar} (local dev). ` +
841...       `Declare the secret under the top-level "secrets:" block in app.yml (see README → Secrets).`,
842...   )
843... }
844... 
845... // --- OAUTH2 tokens ---
846... //
847... // In SPCS the runtime mounts an OAUTH2 secret's (auto-rotated) access token at
848... // /secrets/<name>/access_token, so we read that file fresh on every call. Locally
849... // there is no mount and the token expires after a few minutes, so the app mints and
850... // refreshes tokens itself via the OAuth2 client-credentials grant, caching them in
851... // memory until shortly before they expire.
852... 
853... interface CachedOAuthToken {
854...   token: string
855...   /** Epoch ms after which the cached token must be refreshed. */
856...   expiresAtMs: number
857... }
858... 
859... /** Refresh a cached token this many ms before it actually expires. */
860... const OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS = 60_000
861... /** Fallback lifetime (ms) when the token endpoint omits `expires_in`. */
862... const OAUTH_DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 300_000
863... 
864... const oauthTokenCache = new Map<string, CachedOAuthToken>()
865... // De-dupe concurrent refreshes for the same secret so we mint one token, not N.
866... const oauthInflight = new Map<string, Promise<string>>()
867... 
868... /** Mint a fresh access token via the OAuth2 client-credentials grant and cache it. */
869... async function fetchClientCredentialsToken(name: string, tokenUrl: string): Promise<string> {
870...   const clientId = process.env[secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_CLIENT_ID")]
871...   const clientSecret = process.env[secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET")]
872...   const scope = process.env[secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_SCOPE")]
873... 
874...   const body = new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: "client_credentials" })
875...   if (clientId) body.set("client_id", clientId)
876...   if (clientSecret) body.set("client_secret", clientSecret)
877...   if (scope) body.set("scope", scope)
878... 
879...   const res = await fetch(tokenUrl, {
880...     method: "POST",
881...     headers: { "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
882...     body,
883...   })
884...   if (!res.ok) {
885...     const detail = await res.text().catch(() => "")
886...     throw new Error(
887...       `OAuth2 secret "${name}": token endpoint ${tokenUrl} returned ${res.status} ${res.statusText}. ${detail.slice(0, 300)}`,
888...     )
889...   }
890...   const json = (await res.json()) as { access_token?: string; expires_in?: number }
891...   if (!json.access_token) {
892...     throw new Error(`OAuth2 secret "${name}": token endpoint response contained no access_token.`)
893...   }
894...   const ttlMs = typeof json.expires_in === "number" ? json.expires_in * 1000 : OAUTH_DEFAULT_TTL_MS
895...   oauthTokenCache.set(name, { token: json.access_token, expiresAtMs: Date.now() + ttlMs })
896...   return json.access_token
897... }
898... 
899... /** Local-dev OAuth token: cached client-credentials token (auto-refreshed) or a static env token. */
900... async function getLocalOAuthToken(name: string): Promise<string> {
901...   const cached = oauthTokenCache.get(name)
902...   if (cached && Date.now() < cached.expiresAtMs - OAUTH_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS) {
903...     return cached.token
904...   }
905... 
906...   const tokenUrl = process.env[secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_TOKEN_URL")]
907...   if (tokenUrl) {
908...     // De-dupe concurrent refreshes so a burst of requests mints a single token.
909...     let inflight = oauthInflight.get(name)
910...     if (!inflight) {
911...       inflight = fetchClientCredentialsToken(name, tokenUrl).finally(() => oauthInflight.delete(name))
912...       oauthInflight.set(name, inflight)
913...     }
914...     return inflight
915...   }
916... 
917...   // Escape hatch for quick local testing: a static token (NOT auto-refreshed — it will expire).
918...   const staticToken = process.env[secretEnvVarName(name, "ACCESS_TOKEN")]
919...   if (staticToken) return staticToken
920... 
921...   throw new Error(
922...     `OAuth2 secret "${name}" is not available locally. Set ` +
923...       `${secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_TOKEN_URL")} + ${secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_CLIENT_ID")} + ` +
924...       `${secretEnvVarName(name, "OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET")} for the client-credentials refresh flow ` +
925...       `(recommended — auto-refreshes), or ${secretEnvVarName(name, "ACCESS_TOKEN")} for a short-lived ` +
926...       `static token (see README → Secrets).`,
927...   )
928... }
929... 
930... /** Resolve an OAuth2 access token: SPCS mounted file (auto-rotated) first, else app-level flow. */
931... async function readOAuth2Token(name: string): Promise<string> {
932...   const mounted = readMountedSecretFile(name, "access_token")
933...   if (mounted !== null) return mounted
934...   return getLocalOAuthToken(name)
935... }
936... 
937... /**
938...  * Read a Snowflake SECRET value at runtime.
939...  *
940...  * Use this helper rather than reading `SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_*` env vars yourself or
941...  * querying the SECRET object directly (e.g. `SYSTEM$GET_SECRET`) — a direct
942...  * runtime query is insecure and is not supported.
943...  *
944...  * The secret must be declared under a `secrets:` block in `app.yml` so the runtime
945...  * mounts it. `secrets:` is a TOP-LEVEL key (a sibling of `install:`/`run:`/
946...  * `profile:`) — do NOT nest it under `run:`, or it is ignored:
947...  *
948...  *   secrets:                  # top-level, NOT under run:
949...  *     - name: API_KEY
950...  *       secret: db.schema.api_key_secret
951...  *
952...  * Resolution (mounted file first, then local-dev fallback):
953...  *   - GENERIC_STRING → /secrets/<name>/secret_string   | SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_SECRET_STRING
954...  *   - PASSWORD       → /secrets/<name>/username         | SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_USERNAME
955...  *                      /secrets/<name>/password         | SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_PASSWORD
956...  *   - OAUTH2 (async) → /secrets/<name>/access_token in SPCS (mounted, auto-rotated). Locally the
957...  *                      app mints + refreshes tokens via the OAuth2 client-credentials grant using
958...  *                      SNOWFLAKE_SECRET_<NAME>_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL / _OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / _OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
959...  *                      (+ optional _OAUTH_SCOPE), caching until just before expiry. `getSecret`
960...  *                      returns a `Promise<string>` for OAUTH2 — `await` it.
961...  *
962...  * @example
963...  *   const apiKey = getSecret("API_KEY", SecretType.GENERIC_STRING)
964...  *   const { username, password } = getSecret("DB_CREDS", SecretType.PASSWORD)
965...  *   const token = await getSecret("MY_OAUTH", SecretType.OAUTH2)
966...  */
967... export function getSecret(name: string, type: SecretType.GENERIC_STRING): string
968... export function getSecret(name: string, type: SecretType.PASSWORD): PasswordSecret
969... export function getSecret(name: string, type: SecretType.OAUTH2): Promise<string>
970... export function getSecret(name: string, type: SecretType): string | PasswordSecret | Promise<string>
971... export function getSecret(
972...   name: string,
973...   type: SecretType,
974... ): string | PasswordSecret | Promise<string> {
975...   switch (type) {
976...     case SecretType.GENERIC_STRING:
977...       return readSecretField(name, "secret_string", "SECRET_STRING")
978...     case SecretType.PASSWORD:
979...       return {
980...         username: readSecretField(name, "username", "USERNAME"),
981...         password: readSecretField(name, "password", "PASSWORD"),
982...       }
983...     case SecretType.OAUTH2:
984...       return readOAuth2Token(name)
985...     default:
986...       throw new Error(`Unsupported secret type: ${String(type)}`)
987...   }
988... }
989... 
990... // --- Pool lifecycle ---
991... 
992... /**
993...  * Gracefully drain and destroy all active connection pools.
994...  * Call during server shutdown for clean resource cleanup.
995...  */
996... export async function closePool(): Promise<void> {
997...   const drainPromises: Promise<void>[] = []
998... 
999...   if (ownersPool) {
1000...     const p = ownersPool
